correctness.rationale: The one-vacancy state has exact Bellman cost Q=A*D/[1-t(1-rho)], since a vacancy must last a whole epoch and survives one further epoch with factor t(1-rho). Subtracting exploitation gain d*A from discounted expected vacancy penalty alpha*t*Q gives F_m. Evaluating the two last sizes and cross-multiplying strictly positive denominators yields (n-2)*t*p>2*(1-t). At n=3 the exact signs are -1/40 and +1/10. The embedded exact-fraction program checks 15,840 rational-parameter identities and 260 strict grid witnesses; the general quantifiers rely on the analytic proof. The original excerpt was inspected for the separate permanent-loss baseline.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text inspection of arXiv:2610.21746v1 confirms its analytical theory conditions on no replacement; it notes replacement only in simulations and interpretation, with no finite-pool re-entrance law. Full-text comparison to Joshi (doi:10.1007/s11238-024-10010-2) finds a distinct fear-of-exclusion club formation game. Published-result similarity searches and topical literature searches did not reveal an implication covering the specific sharp finite-outsider formula. Novelty remains conditional on coverage of accessible literature and not a priority certification.
residual_risks: Equivalent unindexed working papers, wider economics texts or standard stochastic renewal models may contain the exact threshold.

value.rationale: The motivating permanent-loss model deduces downward-closed accountability and a maximum size threshold, a mathematically and institutionally meaningful driver of polycentric outcomes. Allowing a full-epoch vacancy with recruitment from the finite outside population breaks the monotone order at the grand-coalition boundary, with necessary-and-sufficient all-n discount/hazard conditions, exact d range, and smallest viable n=3 witness. This is a structural limitation of the published institutional conclusion, not a routine recomputation or arbitrary isolated parameter value.
